summary: Both blocking findings identify existing path inputs that can still point to the deleted worktree during finalize-cleanup. Both require explicit spec coverage before implementation.

items.title: Explicit runtime log path bypasses relocation
items.rationale: `--log-file` is an existing flow-run runtime option and currently bypasses `paths.agentWorkDir`. Leaving it unspecified would let cleanup still write a runtime log under the deleted worktree.
items.evidence: src/lib/dispatcher.js resolveRuntimeLogPath() returns path.resolve(paths.root, input.logFile) before using paths.agentWorkDir. spec.json constraints mention `--log-file` but do not define inside-worktree behavior.

items.title: Configured logger dir bypasses agentWorkDir relocation
items.rationale: `config.logs.dir` is an existing logger path override and currently resolves against the worktree root. Leaving it unspecified would let JSONL logger writes target the deleted worktree even if agentWorkDir is relocated.
items.evidence: src/lib/container.js buildPaths() sets logDir to path.resolve(root, config.logs.dir) when config.logs.dir exists; spec.json constraints currently describe only agentWorkDir relocation.
